correctness.rationale: For h>0, convex scalar perspective h logcosh(z/(2h)) is jointly convex with equality only if the two normalized z/h ratios coincide. The full-support surface-area measure converts equality of integrated F_a at interpolated (a,y) into ratio equality for every normal v. Evaluating at v and −v and subtracting, positive widths imply y0=y1; the remaining equality then forces y=0 or a0=a1. For distinct translations every nonzero Minkowski-interpolation point has F_{aλ}(y)<β, and 0 also lies strictly inside; hence compact strict interior inclusion and Brunn–Minkowski strict nth-root-volume concavity. If K symmetric, F_{tc}(y) is even and strictly convex in t for y,c≠0 since ∂²_h perspective=z² sech²(z/(2h))/(4h³)>0, implying strict radial contraction. Uniform implicit radial differentiation gives ρ_tt(0,u)=−N(u;c)/D(u), D,N>0 and H(c)=∫ρ^{n−1}N/D>0 for c≠0; analytic parity supplies O(t⁴). Domain n≥2, β>0 and C³ positive curvature ensure full normal support and no vanishing h_a; no maximizer existence claimed for nonsymmetric K. Independently confirmed perspective curvature and disk Hessian consistency, not universal numerics.
